- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +10% above recent peak), apply a 1–2 day lag correction to prevent overshoot.  
- If sentiment is consistently low (e.g., 0.0–0.2) and forecast is rising, cap upward movement at 3–5% above recent high to avoid false momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average to correct mean reversion bias.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.2–0.8) and forecast is erratic, smooth transitions by averaging 3–5 consecutive days’ forecast values.
